data_window.source: ClickHouse atlys.promo_coupon_checkout (base), atlys.coupon_funnel_daily_agg, atlys.coupon_discount_daily_agg — all populated with live data

data_caveats: device_type values are inconsistent (ios/android/Desktop/web-user-b2c) — normalized via lower() in queries. 1:1 event-to-user ratio across all event types suggests each user fires each event at most once. FREESHIP has discount_amount=0 (shipping benefit, not price discount). The context contradiction doc (coupon-reject-designed-not-observed.md) claimed zero coupon_rejected rows — that claim is now stale; 268 rejection events are present in the populated data. M3 (conversion lift) computed via base-table self-join on user_id per documented contradiction (coupon-conversion-lift-single-table-gap.md); user_id is not in ORDER BY so the join is a full partition scan.

insights.headline: Coupon apply rate is 27.6% — healthy but with room to grow, since 40% of users enter a code but 31.6% of attempts are rejected
insights.metric_formula: uniqExact(user_id WHERE event='coupon_applied') / uniqExact(user_id WHERE event='coupon_field_shown')
insights.why: The coupon funnel shows strong top-of-funnel engagement: 40.4% of users who see the coupon field attempt to enter a code. However, 31.6% of those who enter are rejected (268 of 848), dragging the net apply rate down to 27.6%. This gap between intent (entry) and success (apply) represents recoverable conversion — improving rejection UX or relaxing entry barriers could push apply rate above 35%. The 47% checkout rate from coupon-field-shown users (987/2100) indicates the checkout flow itself converts well regardless of coupon outcome.
insights.confidence_reason: Exact uniqExact counts from 5,363-row base table; all 2,100 users have 1:1 event ratio. Metric formula matches context doc (coupon-apply-rate.md). Large sample (2,100 users over 21 days).
insights.suggested_next_step: Reduce rejection rate to lift apply rate. Focus on the two actionable reject reasons (min_cart_not_met, already_used) — see I2. Set up daily coupon_apply_rate tile on the PM dashboard using coupon_funnel_daily_agg.

insights.headline: EXPIRED5 code generates 56% of all rejections — retire it or fix it; 'min_cart_not_met' is the #1 reject reason, a pure UX problem
insights.why: EXPIRED5 is clearly a defunct/test code that users are still finding and entering — it accounts for 149 of 268 rejections (55.6%) with all four reject reasons represented equally, suggesting the code triggers multiple validation failures depending on user context. This is pure waste in the funnel. Among the remaining codes, 'min_cart_not_met' is the leading reason — users apply a valid code to a cart below the minimum threshold without knowing the threshold exists. Desktop users have the highest reject rate (39.7%), possibly because desktop checkout shows the coupon field more prominently without context about eligibility. The context contradiction (coupon-reject-designed-not-observed.md) claimed zero coupon_rejected rows — this is now stale; 268 rejection events are confirmed present.
insights.confidence_reason: Exact counts from base table. All 268 rejection events have populated reject_reason and coupon_code. EXPIRED5 dominance is unambiguous (149/268). Context contradiction surfaced and resolved.
insights.contradiction_surfaced: Context doc coupon-reject-designed-not-observed.md (severity: low) claimed zero coupon_rejected rows. This was true at the time of context generation (pre-ingest) but is now stale — 268 rejection events exist. Recommend updating status to 'resolved'.
insights.suggested_next_step: 1) Remove or hide EXPIRED5 from all user-facing surfaces — it generates 56% of rejections with zero successful applies. 2) Add inline validation showing minimum cart requirement BEFORE code entry ('Coupons available for orders above ₹X'). 3) For 'already_used': display a contextual message ('You used this code on [date]'). 4) Update contradiction doc to resolved.

insights.headline: Coupon users convert at 1.54× the rate of non-coupon users (63.1% vs 40.9%) — the strongest lift is on Android at 1.77×
insights.metric_formula: cohort_cvr = uniqExact(user_id where applied>0 AND checked_out>0) / uniqExact(user_id where applied>0 AND saw_field>0); baseline_cvr = same for applied=0; lift = cohort_cvr / baseline_cvr

evidence.method: Base-table self-join on user_id (per contradiction doc: agg cannot express per-user sequencing)

insights.why: The 22.2pp lift is substantial and consistent across all four device types, suggesting genuine coupon-driven conversion rather than a device-specific artifact. Android shows the strongest lift (1.77×) — baseline Android conversion is the lowest at 38.3%, so coupons have the most room to push users over the purchase threshold on that platform. iOS baseline is already higher (43.9%), so the coupon's marginal lift is smaller (1.39×). Caveat: this is observational, not causal — coupon users may be higher-intent to begin with (selection bias). An A/B test with coupon field visibility randomization would establish causation.
insights.confidence_reason: Exact user-level cohort computation from base table via self-join. Selection bias caveat applies — coupon users self-select, so observed lift overstates causal effect. Per-device cuts have adequate sample sizes (44–254 coupon users). Computed per documented M3 formula and contradiction guidance.
insights.contradiction_surfaced: Used base-table self-join for M3 as required by contradiction doc coupon-conversion-lift-single-table-gap.md — the funnel agg's per-stage uniqMerge cannot express per-user sequencing needed for cohort/anti-cohort definitions.
insights.suggested_next_step: Run an A/B test: randomly hide the coupon field for a holdout group to measure causal conversion lift. Android's high lift (1.77×) suggests targeted coupon campaigns for Android users could be high-ROI. Monitor iOS coupon conversion for K1 (OTP autofill regression) effects — if iOS coupon CVR drops while baseline holds, K1 may be interacting with coupon checkout flow.

insights.headline: SUMMER20 drives ₹338,623 in discount cost (42% of total) at a 20% margin erosion rate — controllable since it's one time-bounded campaign
insights.metric_formula: sumMerge(discount_amount_state) GROUP BY coupon_code; erosion = discount / cart_value
insights.why: Margin cost is concentrated and controllable. SUMMER20 alone accounts for 42% of total discount spend (₹338,623) at a fixed 20% rate — consistent with the K6 known-issue documenting the Q2 SUMMER20 campaign. When the campaign ends, this cost drops to zero. ATLYS15 is the second-largest driver (₹234,310, 15% rate) and appears to be a standing promo rather than time-bounded — this is the code to watch for margin discipline. WELCOME (₹300 flat per use at ~5.4% of cart) is low-cost acquisition. FREESHIP is margin-neutral in direct discount terms (₹0 discount_amount), though the operational shipping cost is not captured in this metric.
insights.confidence_reason: Exact sumMerge/countMerge from coupon_discount_daily_agg. Discount percentages match coupon naming (SUMMER20=20%, ATLYS15=15%, FIRST10=10%). Large sample across all codes. FREESHIP ₹0 discount confirmed — it's shipping-only.
insights.suggested_next_step: 1) Set a margin cost alert: if total discount_amount exceeds ₹50K/day, escalate. 2) As SUMMER20 winds down (K6 campaign end), monitor whether ATLYS15 usage increases (substitution effect). 3) Evaluate WELCOME's ROI: ₹300 flat discount × 260 uses = ₹78K — is the new-user LTV payback positive? 4) Consider destination-level caps for high-erosion destinations (TH at 8.7%, AU at 8.0%).

insights.headline: iOS leads volume, Android leads conversion lift, desktop has the worst rejection rate — each platform needs a tailored coupon strategy
insights.metric_formula: apply_rate, reject_rate, conversion_lift, margin_cost GROUP BY device_type, geoip_country_code, destination
insights.why: iOS has the most users (874, 41.6%) and a solid apply rate (29.1%), but its conversion lift is the lowest (1.39×) — iOS users are higher-intent at baseline, so the marginal coupon effect is smaller. Android has the strongest conversion lift (1.77×) but the second-highest rejection rate (34.1%), suggesting Android users attempt more speculative codes. Desktop's 39.7% reject rate is the worst — the desktop coupon field may be too prominent without sufficient eligibility guidance. Geographically, India (60.7% of users) tracks the platform average; GB/AU show slightly elevated apply rates (~31.5%), possibly reflecting higher coupon awareness in those markets. Thailand has the highest margin erosion per destination (8.72% of cart value), likely due to higher-value visa applications attracting percentage-based discounts (SUMMER20).
insights.confidence_reason: Multi-dimensional cuts from both base table and agg tables with adequate sample sizes per segment (minimum 44 users for desktop coupon cohort). Device/geo/destination patterns are consistent across metrics. Turkey's low apply rate (22.6%) is directional only (146 users).
insights.suggested_next_step: 1) Android: highest lift platform — run targeted coupon push notifications to Android users. 2) Desktop: investigate why rejection rate is 40% — add inline eligibility hints. 3) Turkey: lowest apply rate (22.6%) and checkout rate (37%) — evaluate if coupon codes are being distributed in TR market. 4) Thailand: highest margin cost destination (8.7%) — consider destination-level discount caps. 5) Monitor iOS for K1 interaction — if OTP autofill regression hits coupon checkout, iOS coupon CVR may degrade.
